- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 5–10 days of 30d window).
- Forecasts tend to peak too early or overshoot after sharp price spikes in history (e.g., 76+ in 2024-06-26).
- Model underestimates prices in the final 5–10 days of the 30d window, suggesting mean reversion or lagged response.
- Forecasts show persistent bias toward higher values, particularly when history includes recent high prices.
- Model fails to capture downward momentum in price trends after a spike — often underestimates the drop or delays it.
- Forecasts are overly optimistic in the short term (1–5 days) and overly pessimistic in the long term (25–30 days) — suggests horizon mismatch.
- When history includes a sharp decline, model often fails to reflect it until later, creating lagged underestimation.
- Model does not adjust for recent volatility — overestimates stability or smoothness in price paths.
